draft.title: The Guomindang and the Communists
card: The Guomindang (GMD), or Nationalist Party, was led first by Sun Yixian. It aimed to unite China and end foreign influence.
Three Principles
Sun's guide for the GMD: nationalism (a China free of foreign control), democracy (government by the people) and the people's livelihood (a better living for ordinary Chinese).
First United Front
In the 1920s the GMD allowed Communists to join it and worked with them, as both wanted to defeat the warlords and unite China.
1927 split
After Sun died, Jiang Jieshi took over the GMD. In April 1927 in Shanghai, his forces attacked and killed many Communists and union members. This Shanghai Massacre ended the cooperation.
draft.remember: The GMD and Communists united against the warlords until Jiang Jieshi turned on the Communists in 1927.

a.q: What did the GMD and the Communists have in common in the 1920s that led them to work together?
opts: Both wanted to defeat the warlords and unite China
Both wanted to bring back rule by an emperor
Both followed the same Three Principles of Sun Yixian
Both wanted to end the GMD's control of Shanghai
a.why: The warlords had split China, and both parties wanted a united country, so they cooperated. The Three Principles guided the GMD, not the Communists, so shared principles were not the reason.
a.clue: Think about the problem facing China after 1916.

b.q: Which statement best describes the result of the April 1927 Shanghai Massacre?
opts: It ended GMD cooperation with the Communists
It started the alliance between the GMD and Communists
It made Sun Yixian the leader of the GMD
It brought the warlords' rule in China to an end
b.why: Jiang Jieshi's forces killed many Communists and union members, so the two parties stopped working together. It did not start the alliance, which began earlier, and Sun Yixian had already died.
b.clue: Who attacked whom, and what did that do to their partnership?

a.best: Both wanted to defeat the warlords and unite China

b.best: It ended GMD cooperation with the Communists

problems.detail: The why says the Three Principles 'guided the GMD, not the Communists'. This is oversimplified: under the First United Front, Communist members joined the GMD as individuals and formally accepted Sun's Three Principles. The why should say shared principles were not the main reason they cooperated, rather than that the Communists did not follow them at all.

a.q: What did the GMD and the Communists have in common in the 1920s that led them to work together?
opts: Both wanted to defeat the warlords and unite China
Both wanted to bring back rule by an emperor
Both wanted the warlords to keep ruling their regions
Both wanted foreign powers to keep their rights in China
a.why: The warlords had split China, and both parties wanted to defeat them and unite the country, so they cooperated. Communists joined the GMD as individual members and accepted Sun's principles, but this shared aim against the warlords was the main reason for the alliance. Letting foreign powers keep their rights goes against the GMD's aim of nationalism.
a.clue: Think about the problem facing China after 1916.
